hypotheses.paper: theta in R_+^* minus {2 pi}, M = E^{n+2}_theta
hypotheses.note: 0 < α, α ≠ 2π, E^{n+2}_α = Γ_1\(𝔻_∞ × E) of ex:conical (cone angle α, DEC-47), E any finite-dimensional Euclidean space, G = IsomPlus E

questions: l.1619: 'the covering can be endowed with the singular Euclidean metric dr² + r²dθ² + Σdz²' is now proved in coordinates (GX has no Riemannian metric): on {r > 0} the differential of D = (r cos θ, r sin θ, z) at (r, θ, z) sends (ρ, φ, ζ) to w with ‖w₁‖² + ‖w₂‖² = ρ² + r²φ² + ‖ζ‖², i.e. D^*⟨·,·⟩ = dr² + r²dθ² + Σdz_i² (GX.conicalPolar_metric, a conjunct of GX.tame_conical). Every other assertion is proved: sing(M) = π{r=0}, M̃^{sing M} ≅ susp(ℝ) × ℝⁿ over M, D continuous on the whole cover, an a.e. (G,X)-morphism, Γ-equivariant. Does the author accept this coordinate reading of the metric sentence, closing the row?

labels.label: def:topological_space_locally_unloopable
questions: Recorded reading: the paper's 'semi-locally simply connected' (l.1156) is stated for connected spaces, the Lean V carries no connectedness; under local path-connectedness the readings agree, proved as GX.isLocallyUnloopable_iff (equivalently, open path-connected SLSC V) via GX.semilocallySimplyConnected_pathComponentIn.

labels.label: lem:analytical_structure_locally_unloopable

hypotheses.note: no property of G used; only X locally unloopable

hypotheses.paper: M a connected singular (G,X)-manifold (locally connected, T2, second countable)
hypotheses.note: ConnectedSpace, T2Space; FirstCountableTopology, implied by the paper's second countability (weakened)
needed by prop:universality, which the proof's conclusion is; a singular manifold is only locally connected (l.474)

findings: F1 (l.1653–1658): the conclusion 'admits a maximal covering possibly branched over S' is prop:universality (l.1158), whose hypotheses include Y locally path-connected (and §3's first countable, l.810); a singular (G,X)-manifold is only locally connected (def:singular_manifold_locally_connected, l.474) and need not be locally path-connected at its singular points, so the lemma needs 'M locally path-connected' (carried here). The proof's 'unloopable' (l.1656) is undefined; it is read as semilocally simply connected, which is what is proved (with connectedness) for M ∖ S.
questions: Does the §3 standing hypothesis (l.810: all spaces Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable) extend to the 'Singular (G,X)-manifolds (II)' section? If so, lem:analytical_structure_locally_unloopable closes as proved.

labels.label: cor:singular_manifold_skeletal_subset

hypotheses.paper: M a singular (G,X)-manifold, S skeletal ⊇ sing(M), X locally unloopable (l.1660)

hypotheses.note: the hypotheses of prop:universality under which M̃^S is defined; first countability is also carried but is implied by the second countability of a singular manifold (l.474), so it is no strengthening

findings: F3 (l.1693): M̃^S is defined (prop:universality, l.1158) only for M connected (and locally path-connected, first countable); the corollary does not assume M connected. Carried.
questions: Accept 'M connected (and §3's standing hypotheses)' as implicit in the notation M̃^S (as DEC-46 (c) did for g^*A), closing the row?
labels.notes: applied to the extreme BTZ white hole (GX.singular_manifold_skeletal_subset_btz), discharging every hypothesis on a concrete example

kb_proposals: Semilocal simple connectedness is local along open embeddings (GX.semilocallySimplyConnected_of_isOpenEmbedding); charts into a locally unloopable X make every chart-covered open set SLSC (IsLocallyUnloopable.semilocallySimplyConnected_of_charts) — this is how M ∖ S becomes SLSC for prop:universality.

Two maps inducing (G,X)-morphisms from the same atlas into the model differ by one g on a preconnected open set (GX.exists_smul_eq_on_of_isRegularOn, on GX.exists_smul_eq_on_of_isLocalHomeomorphOn of Quotient): the tool for 'no developing map' statements.

For a cylinder Γ_α\(𝔻_∞ × Z), an axis point is singular as soon as the deck generator moves every value of D on {r > 0} (GX.apex_notMem_support_of_smul_ne) — generic in D, so it serves the BTZ/Misner models too.
In GX files nothing opens Real: a bare `π` in a statement is an auto-bound implicit, not Real.pi (it typechecks and then fails to match lemmas); write Real.pi.

To show a singular manifold 'admits no developing map' (def:developing_map l.1729), reduce to the maximal covering by universality: Φ : M̃ → M̂ over M pulls the atlas of M̂ back to M̃'s (eq_aePullback twice), and D̂ ∘ Φ is an a.e. morphism by IsAEMorphismOf.comp (GX.not_admits_developing_btz).

The path component of a point in an SLSC subset is SLSC: a null-homotopy's range is path-connected (ContractibleSpace I from convex_Icc) so it lies in the component; build the restricted Path.Homotopy field by field (GX.semilocallySimplyConnected_pathComponentIn).
